SMTO-EXE-0102 — SMTO didn't repeat a screen request it already handled

GUID: 4065e75c-469b-5a86-81e6-4a15e8095c28
Slug: screen-duplicate
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The Gateway received a screen request it had already handled or cancelled, so it refused to do the same request twice. No new screenshot was taken.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through the task's earlier steps for a screen capture or screen text result that already finished. This message means the same request reached the Gateway twice, so the first attempt may already have what you need.
  2. If you still need the screen, send a new message asking SMTO to take a screenshot or read the screen again. A new message creates a brand-new request, which the Gateway accepts.

What success looks like

  • The new request finishes and the task shows a fresh screenshot or screen text.

If it still fails

  • If every new request is refused this way, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to push the same old request through again; the Gateway is deliberately refusing to repeat it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway screen service refused the request because its execution ID is already active or in the recent finished/cancelled set, so no second observation was made under that ID.

What this means

  • Admission found the screen execution ID in the active or retained finished/cancelled set and refused another observation under that ID. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Admission found the screen execution ID in the active or retained finished/cancelled set and refused another observation under that ID.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original request and its retained receipt instead of treating duplicate rejection as a new screenshot.

How to fix it

  • Each screen.* invocation must carry a unique execution_id; ScreenService.execute in src/gateway_core/screen_service.py rejects IDs found in its active set or its finished/cancelled set (kept for 300 seconds). Inspect the original invocation's receipt and dispatch any further observation as a new tool call instead of replaying the old ID.
  • Use a new deliberate tool invocation. The Gateway does not repeat an already dispatched or cancelled observation ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a new deliberate tool invocation. The Gateway does not repeat an already dispatched or cancelled observation ID.

How to verify the fix

  • The original result is understood and any needed fresh observation has a distinct deliberate invocation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
